lesson_title: The Chief Who Gave Up Being Chief
hook_text: The government said: choose. Be a chief, or fight for freedom. He chose freedom.
clip_script: Groutville, KwaZulu-Natal. A Grade 4 class visits the Luthuli Museum. Albert Luthuli was a teacher, then a chief. In 1952 the government ordered him to leave the ANC or lose his title. He refused, and lost it. He was banned and kept in his village for years. In 1961 he received the Nobel Peace Prize. Dedication: never giving up. Commitment: keeping your promise to others. Sacrifice: giving up something precious for the good of others.
visual_style: Whiteboard road with a fork: one sign says chief, the other says freedom; a figure walks down the freedom road towards a medal.
mood: Serious and admiring, like a story told with respect.
pacing: The choice, the cost, the reward, then the three words.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and think about something you would be willing to give up to help others.
